page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.u1-c1m2.2xlarge is an x86_64 architecture server instance powered by an Intel Xeon CPU running at 2.5 GHz. It features 8 dedicated vCPUs derived from 4 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled, resulting in 2.0 threads per core. The instance is configured with 16.0 GB of system memory, providing a resource density of 2.0 GB per core. It operates on a KVM hypervisor, lacks local storage, and does not include dedicated GPU hardware. Network connectivity is configured with a baseline bandwidth of 2 Gbps.

Benchmark data positions this instance in the average performance tier across multiple standardized tests. The CPU achieved a stress-ng single-core score of 1809.58 and a multi-core score of 7706.71, while the PassMark CPU score reached 10387.28. In memory-bound operations, the instance recorded a read-only small block cached bandwidth of 423.68 GB/sec, which drops to 56.89 GB/sec for uncached large blocks. Cryptographic and vector processing capabilities are supported by hardware flags such as AVX, AVX512F, and AES, yielding a PassMark encryption test score of 4224.31.

The instance exhibits clear performance limitations when handling larger computational models. While small-scale LLM inference using a 135M model runs at 741.79 tokens/sec for prompt processing, performance drops significantly on a medium 7B model, yielding a poor 15.85 tokens/sec for prompt processing and a weak 7.92 tokens/sec for text generation. Large 70B model inference is unsupported. Given these constraints and the lack of local storage, this instance is suited for moderate web serving, software compilation, and database operations that fit within its 16.0 GB memory limit, rather than memory-intensive or large-scale machine learning tasks.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.u1-c1m2.2xlarge is an x86_64 server instance featuring 8 dedicated vCPUs and 16.0 GB of RAM, powered by a 2.5 GHz Intel Xeon processor. Operating on a KVM hypervisor, it lacks local storage and GPU accelerators, relying on a 2 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. Benchmark results place this instance in the average tier, with a PassMark CPU score of 10387.28 and a multi-core stress-ng score of 7706.71. It handles small-scale workloads efficiently, achieving 7.82 million operations per second in Redis SET tests and 9.01 GB/sec in static web serving. However, resource constraints limit its utility for larger tasks; medium-model LLM inference drops to a weak 7.92 tokens/sec for text generation. This instance is best suited for lightweight database operations, software compilation, and moderate web serving.
